one_star_reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with my experience with Holly House Vets following the critical illness and eventual death of my 26-year-old red-eared slider turtle on 26 August 2026.
My turtle had been a patient at Holly House for more than 10 years, and until this experience I had been satisfied with the service I received. The last time she was seen there was in 2022.
At the beginning of August, however, my turtle became critically ill and urgently needed veterinary attention. Over the weekend, I contacted Holly House's out-of-hours service because I was extremely worried and needed emergency help for my reptile. I was told that there was no vet available who could help because they were not experienced with exotic animals. I was instead advised to contact other veterinary practices, including those outside my local area, to find somebody with exotic experience.
As a very worried owner, I found this extremely distressing. I had specifically contacted Holly House because they advertise exotic pet care, and my turtle had been a long-standing patient there.
Thankfully, I eventually found another vet who was willing to see my turtle despite not being an exotic specialist. He did his very best to help her and advised me to contact Holly House again on the next working day because they had medication suitable for reptiles that my turtle need.
When I contacted Holly House on the Monday and explained the situation, I asked for an urgent appointment. During the conversation, I was repeatedly corrected when I referred to an exotic specialist. I was told that Holly House had vets with exotic certification and that they were not specialists. I understand that there is a distinction between being an exotic-certified vet and being a specialist, but my concern was not about terminology — I desperately needed appropriate veterinary care for a critically ill reptile.
I was then offered an appointment on 2 September with an exotic-certified vet. I explained that this was far too late given how seriously ill my turtle was. Sadly, my fears became reality: my precious turtle died on 26 August, before the appointment date.
What has upset me most is that, when Holly House could not provide the emergency care my turtle needed, I was not given meaningful assistance in finding an alternative veterinary service that could treat her urgently. I had to search around myself while dealing with an extremely sick animal.
I appreciate that no veterinary practice can guarantee that an appropriate vet will always be available, and I am not blaming Holly House for the fact that my turtle ultimately died. What I am deeply disappointed by is the lack of urgent support and guidance when I contacted a practice that presents itself as being able to provide care for exotic pets.
My turtle was with me for 26 years, so losing her has been devastating. I will always be grateful to the vet who agreed to see her that weekend and tried his very best to help, despite not having specialist reptile experience.
This experience has completely changed my confidence in relying on Holly House Vets for emergency care on any care for reptiles. I sincerely hope the practice reviews how it supports owners with exotic pets who contact them for urgent or general help.

Throughout my dealings with the sales team, I received information that, from my perspective, was inconsistent and contradictory. I felt that I was repeatedly delayed and that this ultimately prevented me from reserving a property I was seriously considering purchasing.

I am particularly concerned about my dealings with a sales representative named Sarah. When I spoke with Sarah on the day I was attempting to make the reservation, I felt that her manner was unprofessional and that her tone was intimidating. This was particularly disappointing given that I was a serious buyer who was trying to proceed with a property purchase.

On the same occasion, I was told that the police would be contacted, which I found concerning and intimidating in the circumstances.

I also have a serious concern regarding an interaction in which I believe the representative presented herself as another person. I am stating this as my recollection of what happened and would welcome Avant Homes reviewing the relevant records and communications.

I felt that I was not treated fairly or professionally and that the way the situation was handled prevented me from progressing with a purchase.

There are plenty of houses and developers to choose from, and ultimately I have decided to take my business elsewhere. I would rather purchase from a company where I feel prospective customers are treated professionally, communicated with clearly, and can have confidence in the information they are given.

Taking everything I experienced into account, I have personally lost confidence in Avant Homes as a business and have decided that I do not want to proceed with them. I will take my business elsewhere, where I hope to deal with people and a company that I find more professional, transparent and reliable.

I hope those who have purchased at Shann Park have a much more positive experience. Unfortunately, my own experience has left me with serious concerns about the way I was treated as a prospective buyer.

BEWARE: NORTH PROPERTY GROUP WITHHOLDS DEPOSIT MONEY ILLEGALLY.

On 2nd of JULY 2026 my former flatmate and I left the property.

Regarding the deposit, we sent countless email and they went unresponsive for a month, no update whatsoever unless we called them to which they would usually respond with vague and dismissive “we’ll let you know”.

Their justification for the delay was staff being on annual leave, which should not impact the company as much and create massive delays.
I had to open a dispute on The Deposit Scheme website to get the agency’s attention.

On the 13th of AUGUST 2026 ( after one month and half), the agency sent us the proposed deductions which in our opinion were too high, so we refused the deductions and tried to personally negotiate with the agency, per TDS instructions.

On the 21st of AUGUST 2026, the agency had still not reviewed our proposed deductions, however the property manager (L.F.)  had sent us an email confirming the UNDISPUTED amount of deposit has been released and should be in our accounts within 3-7 days.

It is now the 9th of SEPTEMBER 2026, and both me and my flatmate have not got this money back yet. We have contacted the agency by email, with no reply of course. We also called them this week and the previous one, they claim “the money has been released but have no evidence of it, and they’ll be in contact with their accounts department to send us evidence by email”.

I informed The Deposit Scheme about it today, and they said North Property Group has declared they have released the money, which is clearly a lie, and advised me to take legal actions.

Long story short: North Property Group is withholding undisputed deposit money that they owe us and it goes against the law, as agencies must release the undisputed amount within 10 days.

Not only they are committing an illegal act, but they also showed us multiple times they cannot be trusted and they lack communication, consideration and professionalism and we are extremely frustrated with the way they are dealing with us.

I strongly recommend against North Property Group as a tenant if you care about your peace of mind, because it’s incredibly stressful dealing with them but especially if you care about your hard-earned money and you don’t want an agency that withholds your deposit against the law.

Ten minutes.

For two drinks.

There were more than enough crew members working on Monday, so perhaps they were all attending the advanced training course in Watching Drinks Not Get Poured.

Still, I suppose I should be grateful. It takes a certain level of organisational incompetence to make pouring two drinks feel like a major operational undertaking.

And, as I said, this was an emergency refreshment break. Ordinarily, you wouldn’t catch me in a place like this. I have no particular desire to subsidise a multinational chain whose business model is perfectly happy to extract money from communities while contributing to some fairly spectacular public health problems.

So congratulations, McDonald’s. You’ve achieved the remarkable feat of making an already reluctant customer even less likely to return.

I won’t be back anytime soon. You can keep the lukewarm efficiency theatre, the painfully slow service and the thrilling experience of wondering whether your two drinks have entered a different time zone.

Five stars for making me appreciate every other place I could have gone instead.

Unfortunately, I’m extremely disappointed with my recent experience at Allertons, particularly as I have been a regular customer and have also recommended the salon to friends and family in the past.

I initially had my hair done by a lower-level stylist and later returned to have a toner applied. On this occasion, I specifically paid extra to book with a higher-level, more experienced stylist, as I wanted my hair to be noticeably darker.

I made this clear during the consultation. As the stylist was the professional, I trusted her expertise and agreed to her recommendation regarding the toner. However, once my hair was finished, I was disappointed to find that it looked virtually no different from before.

What has made the experience even more frustrating is that, after raising my concerns, I was told that the stylist had informed the manager that I had asked for my hair to look the same. This simply does not reflect the conversation we had. I had specifically explained that I wanted my hair darker. I cannot understand why I would pay to have a toner applied, and pay extra for a more experienced stylist, if my intention was for my hair to look exactly the same afterwards.

I appreciate that hair results can vary and that professional recommendations need to be taken into account, which is precisely why I trusted the stylist’s advice. However, I would expect my original request to be accurately represented when a concern is raised.

Given my experience, I don’t feel that paying extra for a higher-level stylist provided any additional value. As someone who had previously been a loyal customer, alongside friends and family who have also visited the salon, the way this has been handled has been particularly disappointing and off-putting.

Unfortunately, based on this experience, I would not recommend Allertons.
